title: A workspace card could blink to draw the eye when its agent needs the person
body:
A workspace card in the open sidebar shows its agent's state with a coloured stripe on its left edge and a glyph on its state line (`stripe` and `mark` in `src/server/chrome/frame.rs`). The closed sidebar shows a state dot on each tile. Nothing on a card moves, so a workspace that enters `attention` or `done` changes colour and position and nothing more. Jack wants to try a blink or pulse that draws his eye to it.

The only animation in the sidebar today is a point's pulse, in magenta, which lasts up to 30 seconds (decade-e9e1c4 finds it faint on tiles). decade redraws only when something changes, so an animation that never stops means continuous frames for every viewer (see decade-a365b0).

## Proposal

Jack compares several treatments in a web prototype before any is built. The candidates differ in what moves, which states move, and for how long:

- what moves: the stripe, the glyph, the card's background, or an outline round the card
- which states: `attention` only, or `attention` and `done`
- how long: always, or a burst when the state is entered followed by a rare pulse

## Open

- Which treatment, chosen from the prototype.
- How it shows on the closed sidebar's tiles.
- Whether it stops once the person has looked, tied to the timeout in decade-ee05df.
close_reason: Landed in a402a32: done and attention cards breathe toward their dark tint every 1.6 s, except while hovered. Tiles do not breathe.

notes.author: Jack Roddy/7403d304
notes.text: Jack chose treatment 3 from the prototype: the card's background breathes toward a dark tint of its state's colour and back, about 1.6 s a cycle. It redraws the whole card on every frame while it runs. He wants it built together with the glyph button in decade-6969e7. A second prototype pairs the breathing with candidate glyph buttons.
